name: Burgas Airport
before:
Bulgaria's second airport and the one that matters for the southern coast. It serves Burgas and the seaside resorts along that stretch, so summer traffic dominates and the terminal is busiest between June and September.

The building is newer than most clients expect. Terminal 2 opened in December 2013 and replaced a 1950s terminal, and now handles all passenger traffic. It has 31 check in counters, nine security lanes and eight departure gates, with a rated capacity of 2.7 million passengers a year across 21,000 square metres.

Arrivals are split into Schengen and non-Schengen zones with twelve immigration positions and four baggage carousels, which is worth knowing when quoting transfer times for a UK client, since the non-Schengen queue is the one they will join.

The airport is near the Sarafovo neighbourhood, about 10 km from the centre of Burgas.
after:
The airport that matters for Bulgaria's southern coast. It serves Burgas and the seaside resorts along that stretch, so summer traffic dominates and many routes run only in season. On Eurostat's figures it was the country's second busiest airport in 2024 and a close third, just behind Varna, in 2025.

Bulgaria is in the Schengen area, so UK clients go through passport control on arrival, and the FCDO warns that the EU's new Entry/Exit System can mean a longer wait at the border. Worth knowing when quoting transfer times.

The airport is about 10 km from the centre of Burgas.

claims.note: Was 'Bulgaria's second airport'. Eurostat's tables of every Bulgarian airport it reports: 2024 Sofia 7,884,976, Burgas 1,781,239, Varna 1,534,753; 2025 Sofia 8,382,684, Varna 1,851,453, Burgas 1,824,539. The two swap places, so the text gives both years, attributed. The operator's own site refused (403 to a plain request and to the browser) and Fraport's traffic page gives only the two airports together (more than 3.7 million a year). Wikipedia calls it the second largest airport in the country.

claims.claim: the runway rebuilt from November 2025 to April 2026; UK airlines for summer 2026; the Fraport concession
claims.why: Held back: new facts that replace nothing. The operator's release of 23 July 2026 says the runway was fully rehabilitated between November 2025 and April 2026 for more than 60 million euros (the operator alone). Its summer 2026 release lists Jet2 with 11 routes including a new one from Gatwick, easyJet from Manchester and Gatwick, and Wizz Air from Luton (the operator alone). Fraport's own page dates the 40-year concession for Varna and Burgas to 10 September 2006, and Wikipedia's infobox names Fraport Twin Star as operator.
